clue.text: Writer's champion getting a gesture of affection and love

parts.note: a champion is the victor in a contest
a hug is a gesture of affection
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: An author's hero wins a cuddle and some romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Writer' stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo was the French novelist who wrote Les Misérables.

clue.text: Page 5 et al to be rewritten

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: writing something again lets its letters come out in a new order, so et al is rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction that page five, with its list of names, needs redrafting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Page' looks like a page of a book; it is a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a young attendant, and a valet is a personal manservant, so both are kinds of servant.

clue.text: Parisian designer carrying the latest in fashion across this to London

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so the designer's name takes a letter inside

parts.note: Coco Chanel was the Paris fashion designer

indicators.note: the latest part of a word is its final letter, here of fashion

explanation.surface: A French couturier brings the newest styles over to London.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a journey: one goes across the Channel from France to reach London.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Channel is the stretch of sea a traveller from Paris crosses to reach London.

clue.text: Begin talk about one spirit

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for talk surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: to orate is to talk, especially pompously
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Start a conversation about a ghost, or perhaps a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to come into being or to start, a synonym of begin.

clue.text: Glad of July revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters of 'of July' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Happy about a July uprising, like the French one of 1830.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyful and glad are synonyms for feeling pleased and happy.

clue.text: Towel wrapped round a little creature

indicators.note: wrapping the letters round changes their order, so the word towel is rearranged

explanation.surface: A towel bundled around a small animal, as after a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young or small owl, so a little creature.

clue.text: Agile dancing in very loud and skimpy attire

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the musical mark

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the word agile is rearranged

explanation.surface: A nimble dancer performs to loud music in scanty costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A fig leaf, as worn by Adam and Eve in paintings, is the barest of coverings.

clue.text: Endless psalm run? Yes, to be broken by this

definitions.text: Endless psalm run? Yes, to be broken by this

indicators.note: being broken means the trimmed letters fall apart and are reassembled in a new order
endless applies to each of the four words in turn, cutting off the last letter of every one

explanation.surface: A worshipper wonders whether a long psalm will be interrupted by this prayer line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the last letter from each of psalm, run, Yes and to, leaving PSALRUYET, which 'be broken' rearranges. The whole clue also defines the answer, the minister's call that breaks into the singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Let us pray is the minister's call in church services that interrupts the hymns and psalms to begin prayers.

clue.text: Bound to appear in suitable cinema

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be inside it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: fit means suitable
a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: Something certain to show up at an appropriate picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain', but it is a jump. A fleapit is British slang for a shabby old cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleapit is a British slang name for a run-down, grubby cinema.

clue.text: Times coverage of fair Britain

indicators.note: coverage puts one word over another, so the word for times wraps round the other

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in three by four
fair hair or skin is light

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper reports on a fair Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper; it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighty is old British soldiers' slang for Britain, dating from service in India.

clue.text: Stirring an idiot into a reshuffle

parts.note: a git is an idiot in British slang, so 'an idiot' is a git

indicators.note: reshuffling the letters of 'into a' puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: Causing trouble by bringing a fool into a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation is a stirring up, whether of liquid or of public feeling.

clue.text: Like more relaxed soldiers putting up with a tormentor

parts.note: standing something means putting up with it
a tease is someone who torments others playfully

explanation.surface: Troops coping with someone who keeps baiting them.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing at ease is the drill position, feet apart and hands behind, that is more relaxed than attention.

clue.text: See 11
Be blunt with soprano having reportedly settled with a flat in the outskirts of Scunthorpe

parts.note: Maria Callas was the celebrated Greek-American soprano

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is spoken, and the spelling entered follows that sound

parts.note: a settled bill is paid

indicators.note: in places the word for flat between the outer letters of the town
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters, here of Scunthorpe

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home

explanation.walkthrough: 'soprano' is not the usual S but a named singer, Maria Callas, whose surname runs on into the first SPADE. Scunthorpe is an industrial town in Lincolnshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To call a spade a spade is an idiom for speaking plainly and bluntly, without euphemism.

clue.text: Falsified my account in defiance

indicators.note: a falsified account has been cooked, so the letters of 'my account' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cooked the books in open contempt of the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Contumacy is stubborn, wilful disobedience to authority, especially to a court.

clue.text: Norfolk town available in black?

definitions.meaning: A market town in Norfolk, a county in eastern England
read as ..., Henry Ford's Model T, which buyers could famously have in any colour so long as it was black

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as THE T FORD: Ford said customers could have any colour they liked so long as it was black.
explanation.definitionFit: Thetford is a town in Norfolk; split differently it names the Model T Ford, famously only sold in black.

clue.text: Attempt in essay to describe desolation

indicators.note: to describe is to draw round, so the clue words enclose the answer among their letters

explanation.surface: A student tries in an essay to depict bleakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describe' is used in its geometric sense, to trace around something.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptiness, a bleak and barren state, is a synonym of desolation.

clue.text: One's done no wrong in historical 23 shindig?

parts.note: 23 across is VATICAN; Innocent was the name of thirteen popes in history
a shindig is a lively party

explanation.surface: Was a celebration at the Vatican, held by a pope, entirely blameless?
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 23 points to the Vatican, so the historical figure is a pope named Innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: The innocent party in a dispute or divorce is the person who has done nothing wrong.

clue.text: Stock unit many stripped from university

parts.note: Oxo is a British brand of stock cube

indicators.note: stripping a word removes its outer letters, leaving the middles of unit and many

explanation.surface: A farmer or broker strips a unit of many beasts away from a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock unit' reads as one phrase, but the stock is OXO, a brand of stock cubes sold in Britain, and 'unit' is stripped along with 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxonian is a member or graduate of Oxford University, so someone from that university.

parts.note: A1 means first class, written AI
lager is a beer

explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are ceremonial robes and insignia, so a kind of formal finery or fancy dress.

clue.text: State of antivac movement

clue.text: Unexpectedly choke, having eaten meal on vacation that contains poison

explanation.walkthrough: 'that contains' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemlock is a poisonous plant, and the poison drawn from it famously killed Socrates.

clue.text: One dry cocktail there

explanation.surface: Pointing out a dry martini over at the bar.
